Senses.Explanation: Literally, "one-finger Chan." The phrase names Juzhi's recorded use of a raised finger in public interviews. A later record states the visible rule directly: "Whenever someone came, Master Juzhi only extended one finger; he called it one-finger Chan" (俱胝和尚逢人但伸一指頭，喚做一指頭禪). In the transmitted case, Tianlong raises one finger to Juzhi; afterward, whenever students ask, Juzhi raises one finger, and before dying he says, "I obtained Tianlong's one-finger Chan; through my whole life I could not use it up" (吾得天龍一指頭禪，一生用不盡). The record also preserves criticism rather than making the label an unquestioned formula: Xuansha says he would have broken the finger, Caoshan faults Juzhi's taking it up, and Sanshan asks, "What connection does one-finger Chan have? It cheated that monk and buried him alive his whole life" (一指頭禪有甚交涉？賺殺阿僧終身活埋). Its Chan-specific bend is thus a named, publicly repeated response inherited from Tianlong and continually examined by later masters.
Senses.Note: Attested 80 times in 50 allowlisted texts. "Juzhi's one finger" (俱胝一指) names the case/action family; "one-finger Chan" (一指頭禪) is the label Juzhi claims for what he received from Tianlong. The same referent is praised, questioned, and criticized; differing appraisals are readings of one recorded deployment, not separate senses.

Occurrences.Kwic: 俱胝和尚逢人但伸一指頭，喚做一指頭禪。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yunxi Langting Ting (雲溪俍亭挺禪師語錄), in Langting Jingting's instruction to the attendant Qianyun. Langting Jingting retells the old one-finger case; Juzhi is the exact narrated actor who extends one finger whenever he meets someone and calls it one-finger Chan (俱胝和尚逢人但伸一指頭，喚做一指頭禪). The attendant, Juzhi's boy, and the later quoted Caoshan appraisal do not speak or perform this stored sentence.

Occurrences.Kwic: 吾得天龍一指頭禪，一生用不盡。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Collected Old Cases Raised in the Lineage (宗門拈古彙集), Juzhi section. Juzhi is the exact speaker of his closing claim that he received Tianlong's one-finger Chan and did not use it up in a lifetime.

Occurrences.Kwic: 後凡有所問。只豎一指。每曰。我得天龍一指頭禪。一生受用不盡。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Dahui Pujue (大慧普覺禪師語錄). In Dahui Zonggao's retelling, Juzhi is the exact actor who thereafter raises one finger whenever questioned and says, 'I obtained Tianlong's one-finger Chan; I have used it inexhaustibly my whole life.'

Occurrences.Kwic: 一指頭禪有甚交涉？賺殺阿僧終身活埋。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Sanshan Lai (三山來禪師語錄): in his old-case comment, Sanshan Denglai asks what connection one-finger Chan has, says it buried the monk Juzhi alive for his whole life, and asks how many later finger-raisers actually received its use.

Occurrences.Kwic: 一指頭禪誰不有？靈樞妙轉在天龍
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Collected Old Cases Raised in the Lineage (宗門拈古彙集), Juzhi section. Muchen Daomin, introduced inline as Tiantong Min (天童忞), is the exact commentator and verse speaker who asks who does not have one-finger Chan and locates its deft turning in Tianlong.
